summary: XMPP is broad on features but low on demonstrated foothold: STARTTLS posture, IBR form availability, SASL ANONYMOUS actual bind (T2 with anon_jid), weak-SASL advertisement, s2s dialback posture, XEP-0092 sw-version pull, XEP-0030 disco components, legacy-TLS cert grab, cert-mismatch check. enum_muc_rooms and xmpp_muc_public_rooms narrative exist but findings() never emits xmpp_muc_public_rooms — dead-emit gap. No SCRAM/PLAIN authenticated brute against advertised mechs; no IBR actual account creation (only form-availability check); anon_bind isn't chained into disco/roster to enumerate real accounts.

findings.title_pattern: XMPP STARTTLS not offered (cleartext stream) / not required
findings.tier_evidence: stream:features actually parsed; absence of <starttls/> or of its <required/> is deterministic.
findings.promotion_notes: Once cleartext, sniff live PLAIN auth (tcpdump for base64 in <auth mechanism='PLAIN'>...</auth>) to capture credentials. Requires network position.
findings.tester_next_step: tcpdump -i any -A -s 0 'tcp port 5222' | grep -B2 -A2 mechanism=.PLAIN; base64 -d to reveal user\0user\0pass.

findings.tier_evidence: IBR form returned to unauth iq get proves the endpoint accepts registration — but no account actually created yet.
findings.promotion_notes: Actually submit the registration form (iq set with username/password) to create a live account = T3 foothold with authenticated JID. Push new JID into known_credentials for downstream MUC / roster / adhoc probes. Currently only GETs the form.
findings.tester_next_step: Send <iq type='set' id='r2'><query xmlns='jabber:iq:register'><username>recce</username><password>Recce!Pw1</password></query></iq> to <domain>; then SASL SCRAM as recce and dump roster.

findings.tier_evidence: Actual SASL ANONYMOUS <success/> received and JID bound — recce holds an authenticated session (anonymous account). anon_jid captured.
findings.promotion_notes: Anon-bind session is already an authenticated foothold. Extend probe to (a) iq get jabber:iq:roster (usually empty for anon), (b) disco#items to server to walk components, (c) presence to a public MUC to join. Wire session into a session store so other XMPP-derived probes reuse it.
findings.tester_next_step: python -c 'via slixmpp anonymous bind then send disco#items to conference.<domain>'; then send <presence to='public-room@conference.<domain>/recce'/> to join & lurk.

findings.tier_evidence: Advertisement of PLAIN/LOGIN on cleartext or DIGEST-MD5 anywhere is deterministic and only fires when the weak set is really offered.
findings.promotion_notes: Combine with cleartext to sniff PLAIN. For DIGEST-MD5, do a bounded challenge/response replay attack — request challenge, compute response for candidate PSK, submit; hit == T2 auth.
findings.tester_next_step: tcpdump 'tcp port 5222' + base64-decode PLAIN blobs; or hydra -L users.txt -P passwords.txt xmpp://<ip>

findings.promotion_notes: Actual dialback spoof requires DNS control over an inbound domain — script the DNS + dialback exchange from a controlled peer to prove federation identity forgery.
findings.tester_next_step: From a controlled domain: open s2s to <target>:5269, send <db:result to='<target>' from='attacker.example'>KEY</db:result>, observe accept — proves spoofable federation.

findings.title_pattern: XMPP service discovery reveals server components
findings.tier_evidence: disco#items + per-item disco#info actually walked; component JIDs (muc/http_upload/proxy65/pubsub) and identities/features captured — real data.
findings.promotion_notes: For http_upload components, issue XEP-0363 slot request and PUT a canary — foothold via authenticated file host. For proxy65 issue bytestreams initiation to test relay abuse. For MUC, enum public rooms (enum_muc_rooms already implemented but not wired).
findings.tester_next_step: Feed each component JID: <iq type='get' to='upload.<domain>'><request xmlns='urn:xmpp:http:upload:0' filename='r.txt' size='4' content-type='text/plain'/></iq>; PUT canary to returned URL.

findings.tier_evidence: enum_muc_rooms() actually lists rooms with password_protected/hidden/members_only flags — real data. GAP: findings() never emits this kind, only NARRATIVE exists; enum is dead-called.
findings.promotion_notes: Wire enum_muc_rooms into the analyze() flow so findings() can emit it. Then join open rooms with the anon JID to sniff subject/traffic — internal team names / project codewords typically leak in room subjects.
findings.tester_next_step: First fix findings() to emit the kind. Then join open room: send <presence to='room@conference.<domain>/recce'/> and observe subject/roster.

findings.promotion_notes: Fingerprint-only; cert_mismatch is the deeper probe.

findings.tier_evidence: iq get jabber:iq:version returned parsed name/version/os — real product+firmware bytes pulled without auth (or via anon session).
findings.promotion_notes: Key CVE mapper on (name,version) tuples: Openfire CVE-2023-32315 admin console traversal → RCE; ejabberd CVE-2021-33036 auth bypass; Prosody mod_s2s CVEs. Auto-run CVE-2023-32315 probe (GET /setup/setup-s/*) when Openfire seen — T3 primitive.
findings.tester_next_step: For Openfire: curl -k 'https://<ip>:9090/setup/setup-s/../../../log.jsp' — CVE-2023-32315 exposure; then vendor-specific PoC.

findings.title_pattern: XMPP server fingerprinted (product from stream error)
findings.tier_evidence: Product substring in stream:error — pure fingerprint.
findings.promotion_notes: Same as sw_version but weaker signal; feed to CVE mapper when version is missing.
findings.tester_next_step: Trigger stream error with bogus 'to' and read <text> body.

findings.title_pattern: XMPP legacy-TLS cert does not match stream 'from' domain
findings.promotion_notes: MitM primitive against non-pinning clients — realistic only with network position; can't be tier-promoted without on-path capability.
findings.tester_next_step: On-path: bettercap sslstrip against 5223 client traffic (rare in prod, common in isolated labs).
